XI. Discussion of Problems and Objectives Raised and HUD Accommadation
1. General
The following paragraph contain a discussion and/or answer to specific question and points raised by the various agencies commenting on the Draft Environmental Statement. A copy of each comment is contained in the annex to this chapter in the order in which it is discussed. Comments which are general in nature and for which a specific response would be difficult to formulate, are addressed, to the extent possible in the text of this Final Environmental Statement. Specific changes in the text are noted in the following discussions. Substantiation comments and questions from the text of the various comments are capsulized for brevity; however, they are sufficient to identify the specific item in the commenting document.
2. Comments and Responses 
a. United States Environmental Protection Agency
(1) Comment: Identify 10, 50 and 100 year flood plain. 
Response: Appendix A indicates the 100 year flood plain and the flood record. A further delineation of the flood plain area by 10 year or 50 y ear levels is not available at this time; therefore, they cannot be demonstrated in this final report. However, the Federal Insurance Administration (FIA) is conducting a study, coordinated through the Susquehanna River Basin Commission, to provide this information along with the establishment of "Floodways". This information will not be available until May of 1974. Parties interested in this information should contact the River Basin Commission around that date. (see corrected text in last paragraph of page 49).
(2) Comment: Flood Plain not to be treated as a homogenous area. 
Response: The current Flood Plain Ordinance bing considered for adoption by the city of Harrisburg contains language that will permit individual treatment of properties based on varrying degrees of flood danger; however, it is not related to specific areas such as 10, 50 or 100 year Flood Plain Areas.
